update_log: Complete updated baseline of all official UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India categorized by Cultural, Natural, and Mixed sites for the 2026 Exam Cycle.

cultural_sites.site_name: Moidams – the Mound-Burial System of the Ahom Dynasty
cultural_sites.significance: Late medieval mound-burial system of the Tai-Ahom dynasty, representing unique royal funerary traditions akin to the pyramids of Egypt.
Established by Rabindranath Tagore; an experimental school and university (Visva-Bharati) based on concepts of nature-based learning and global humanism.
Includes the Chennakeshava, Hoysaleswara, and Keshava temples; highly unique for their star-shaped architectural plans and hyper-detailed soapstone carvings.
One of the most remarkable archaeological sites of the Indus Valley Civilization; famous for its advanced water harvesting system and stone fortifications.
Built during the Kakatiya period using lightweight 'floating bricks'; features incredibly intricate polished black basalt carvings and brackets.
A fortified city planned in 1727 under Sawai Jai Singh II, designed using Vedic architectural principles (Vastu Shastra) and grid iron patterns.

cultural_sites.site_name: Victorian Gothic and Art Deco Ensembles of Mumbai
cultural_sites.significance: A collection of 19th-century Victorian Neo-Gothic public buildings and 20th-century Art Deco residential buildings flanking the Oval Maidan.

cultural_sites.site_name: The Archaeological Site of Nalanda Mahavihara
cultural_sites.significance: Remains of a major monastic and scholastic institution dating from the 3rd century BCE to the 13th century CE; the ancient world's premier residential university.
An exceptional multi-storey subterranean stepped well built by Queen Udayamati; designed as an inverted temple honoring Lord Vishnu.

cultural_sites.location: Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Sawai Madhopur, Jhalawar, Jaipur, and Jaisalmer (Rajasthan)
cultural_sites.significance: Six majestic forts representing the defensive, military, and courtly architecture of Rajput princely states between the 8th and 18th centuries.
An astronomical observation site built by Maharaja Jai Singh II; houses the world's largest stone sundial (Vrihat Samrat Yantra).
Constructed by Shah Jahan; represents the absolute peak of Mughal architectural creativity and royal palace complex design.
Concentrated, unexcavated Hindu-Jain ruins alongside a 16th-century Islamic capital city, displaying a rare transition of architectural styles.

cultural_sites.site_name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (formerly Victoria Terminus)
cultural_sites.significance: An outstanding example of Victorian Gothic Revival architecture in India blended with themes derived from traditional Indian palace designs.
Five clusters of natural rock shelters displaying prehistoric cave paintings that span from the Paleolithic and Mesolithic periods up to the historical era.

cultural_sites.site_name: Mahabodhi Temple Complex at Bodh Gaya
cultural_sites.significance: One of the earliest brick structures surviving from the late Gupta period; directly marks the location where Lord Buddha achieved supreme enlightenment.
The first grand garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent; served as the structural inspiration and prototype for the Taj Mahal.
Features the 73-meter brick minaret, Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque, and the rust-free iron pillar of Chandragupta II.
A complex of stupas, pillars, and monasteries; the Great Stupa is the oldest stone structure in India, commissioned by Ashoka.
Rock-cut cave temples primarily dedicated to Lord Shiva; famous for the colossal 7-meter high Trimurti sculpture.

cultural_sites.location: Thanjavur, Gangaikonda Cholapuram, and Darasuram (Tamil Nadu)
cultural_sites.significance: Includes Brihadisvara, Gangaikondacholisvaram, and Airavatesvara temples; brilliant examples of Chola architecture, sculpture, and bronze casting.
Features a striking blend of Northern (Nagara) and Southern (Dravidian) temple architectural styles built under the Chalukya Dynasty.
Includes the Basilica of Bom Jesus (housing the relics of St. Francis Xavier); instrumental in spreading Manueline and Baroque art styles across Asia.
The short-lived capital city built by Emperor Akbar; features grand structures like the Buland Darwaza and Jama Masjid.
The opulent ruins of the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire; showcases advanced Dravidian civic, military, and religious architecture.
Built by the Chandela Dynasty; features a harmonious balance of Hindu and Jain temples famous for their Nagara shikharas and expressive erotic sculptures.
Built by Pallava kings; features rock-cut cave rathas (chariots), mandapas, the open-air relief 'Descent of the Ganges', and the stone Shore Temple.
A masterpiece of Kalinga architecture built by King Narasimhadeva I; shaped as a monumental stone chariot for Surya, the Sun God.
A massive 16th-century red sandstone walled city built by Akbar, serving as the primary seat of the Mughal Emperors until 1648.
30 rock-cut Buddhist caves containing masterpieces of ancient fresco paintings and sculptures dating from the 2nd century BCE.
34 rock-cut structures honoring Buddhism, Hinduism, and Jainism; contains Cave 16, the monumental monolithic Kailash Temple.
An iconic white marble mausoleum constructed under Shah Jahan; widely revered as the absolute pinnacle of Mughal artistic achievement.
Three narrow-gauge hill railways representing brilliant engineering solutions to establishing regular rail links across rugged mountain terrains.

cultural_sites.site_name: The Architectural Work of Le Corbusier
cultural_sites.significance: The Complexe du Capitole in Chandigarh, recognized as an outstanding global contribution to the Modern Movement in architecture.

natural_sites.site_name: Great Himalayan National Park Conservation Area
natural_sites.significance: Characterized by high alpine peaks, meadows, and riverine forests; acts as a crucial refuge for endangered species like the snow leopard and Western Tragopan.

natural_sites.location: Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Kerala
natural_sites.significance: Older than the Himalayas; a global biodiversity hotspot containing exceptionally high levels of endemism in its montane forest ecosystems.
The world's largest area of mangrove forests, formed by the delta of the Ganga, Brahmaputra, and Meghna rivers; primary habitat of the Bengal Tiger.
A man-made wetland reserve that serves as a highly critical wintering ground for thousands of rare and endangered migratory waterfowl and birds.
Located in the foothills of the Himalayas; shelters unique and endangered endemic wildlife like the Pygmy Hog, Assam Roofed Turtle, and Golden Langur.
Undisturbed tall elephant grass meadows and swamps; home to the world’s largest population of the Great Indian One-horned Rhinoceros.

natural_sites.site_name: Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers National Parks
natural_sites.significance: Comprises the rugged wilderness of Nanda Devi peak alongside the Valley of Flowers, globally renowned for its meadows of endemic alpine flowers.

mixed_sites.significance: India's only Mixed site. Features spectacular high-altitude landscapes centering around Mt. Khangchendzonga, embedded deep within unique Buddhist cultural myths and local folklore.
